revisions.title: A Local Frame
revisions.body: Keep the emphasis local: this opening frames the immediate exchange without projecting later stakes onto it.

revisions.title: The Aim of Inquiry
revisions.body: At 279a–282e, Socrates contrasts the pursuit of wisdom with eristic display, directing attention to wisdom rather than to argument as a contest.

revisions.title: The Sophist’s Inference
revisions.body: Dionysodorus presents the friends’ concern for Cleinias as implying a wish for his death; Ctesippus rejects that inference. The force of the exchange lies in treating an apparent implication as though it were an established fact, then exposing the overreach.

revisions.title: From Having to Using
revisions.body: Socrates shifts the test from possession to use: goods help only when knowledge directs their use.

revisions.title: The completed wisdom sentence
revisions.body: The sentence on wisdom is complete; the passage does not establish a reaction to the display.
